correctness.rationale: Independently solving the sticky-state equations in midpoint coordinates gives an allocation-dependent part of M/T equal to 2(1+eta)((lambda+1)h^2+wh)/(4eta+F(1-h^2)), up to an h-independent constant. In detail, take l=beta(1+h)/2, r=beta(1-h)/2, delta=(m_+(L/2)-m_-(L/2))/T, and Q the mean of the two dimensionless wall orientation averages minus 1/2. The boundary equations are lQ-[eta+(lambda+1)l/2]delta=1+eta and rQ+[eta+(lambda+1)r/2]delta=1+eta. Their determinant is eta beta+(lambda+1)lr>0 even at zero allocation to one wall. Differentiating the resulting mean gives the asserted prefactor and P(h)=2(lambda+1)Hh+w(H+Fh^2). Its derivative is at least 8eta(lambda+1), and its two endpoint signs are strictly negative/positive even at |w|=lambda+1. The displayed stable root, strict interiority, oddness and monotonicity follow. Finite mean at zero allocation on one side follows from a uniform positive chance in bounded time to reach and be killed at the active wall: use runs without tumbles and, if needed, a bounded wait for release from the opposite sticky state. The frozen proof and checker support the model; the script was inspected, not run, and the recorded simulation is not used.
residual_risks: The conclusion is confined to common positive release, a fixed sum of constant exponential killing rates, and interior initial position. It does not assert an optimum for unequal release rates, other wall models, or arbitrary survival objectives.

value.rationale: A fixed amount of wall reactivity is a natural design constraint and makes all-at-one-wall choices plausible for strongly polarized or off-center starts. The theorem excludes both extreme allocations uniformly, gives an explicit optimum, and identifies how location and heading compensate. This is a complete design answer rather than an enumeration or a relabeled exit-time formula.
residual_risks: No practical claim under anisotropic or non-exponential wall physics, and no finite-horizon ordering, is implied.
